findings.failure_path: An agent encounters an earlier higher-authority safety instruction and a contradictory instruction later in the prompt. The new absolute statement that the nearer-to-end instruction wins directs it toward the later instruction, ignoring authority precedence and enabling a safety or contract bypass.
findings.smallest_fix: Qualify positional resolution as applying only to conflicting peer instructions at the same authority level when no explicit precedence exists, and state that system/developer and other established authority boundaries always take priority.

findings.failure_path: This non-wording shared-skill change can be released from the supplied packet with only prose and inaccessible external links; no behavior-sensitive evidence demonstrates that a domain-specific destructive rule is now generalized instead of discarded, or that the withdrawn mechanism does not regress existing consolidation behavior. A static review can therefore remain green while the intended precedence never fires.
findings.smallest_fix: Add the required recorded behavioral evidence: at minimum a true RED baseline and replay where the old rule discards a domain-specific safety invariant and the new rule preserves it through generalization, plus semantic-control evidence for obligations intended to remain unchanged. Include bounded source evidence or narrow the unsupported universal and quantitative claims.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The local keep-versus-discard precedence is coherent, but the new mechanism overstates positional conflict resolution without limiting it to same-authority instructions.
The unqualified later-instruction-wins rule can be misapplied across trust or authority levels, potentially treating a later unsafe instruction as overriding an earlier safety constraint.
The diff does not constrain how conflict resolution behaves when instructions differ in authority; this leaves a credible unsafe decision path.
No RED baseline, behavioral replay, semantic-control result, or source excerpt is supplied for these non-wording shared-gate changes, so the required evidence check cannot be completed.
The replacement substantially enlarges a single mid-file rule and introduces broad, benchmark-dependent claims, increasing ambiguity and maintenance burden.
The Markdown change is reversible and needs no data migration, but its own shared-skill gate requires behavioral evidence before release and none is present.
There is no operational telemetry impact, but the packet lacks the recorded evidence needed to diagnose whether the changed skill behavior actually fires.
The high-risk boundary is a widely shared instruction-resolution gate; authority-aware precedence and behavior-sensitive evidence are both required before it can be considered contained.
